growth_signal.value: Says its annual distribution volume now exceeds ¥2 billion (about $13M).

raised.value: ¥120M Series A (about $780K); ¥440M raised in total including loans

entry.idea: Hospitals and pharmacies often end up with surplus medicine they cannot use before it expires, while other facilities nearby are short, so 9lione runs a platform that moves that surplus medicine to the places that need it.
entry.lesson: When a regulated market wastes a valuable resource through ad hoc manual trades, get the license yourself and turn the informal trading into a real marketplace.
entry.name: 9lione

growth.basis: number: annual distribution volume exceeding ¥2 billion ($13M)
growth.reason: An annual distribution volume above ¥2 billion is a real number, but there is no year-over-year comparison to show the pace of growth.

market.reason: Redistributing surplus medicine is a real need, but it is limited to Japan's own pharmaceutical distribution rules and market.

tech.reason: Getting a pharmaceutical wholesaler license and running GDP-compliant tracking is a real barrier to copying it fast, but the core marketplace idea could still be matched by another licensed player in a year or two.

entry.twist: It holds its own official pharmaceutical wholesaler license and carries the stock itself, handling quality control and delivery under Japan's distribution rules, rather than just running a listing site, and it is now adding AI to predict demand and keep prices fair.
entry.who_pays: Hospitals and pharmacies that buy or sell surplus medicine through the platform.
entry.why_now: Japan has ongoing shortages of some medicines, so getting unused stock from where it sits idle to where it is actually needed has become both a cost problem and a health problem.
